summary: The six-state Y-basis convention (`U_Y ⊗ U_Y*`) and the Werner/twirling math are consistent with the stated formulation, and the decoy rate composition itself is standard. The patch is still not Phase-0 acceptable: `out_of_scope` protocols are not actually blocked from the solver, the MDI implementation is marked `covered` even though the multi-source MS-EB API is broken, and the fallback numerical routines mishandle feasibility/infeasibility in ways that weaken the scientific guarantees claimed in the docs and report.

issues.description: `wlc_key_rate()` never checks `protocol.scope_tag`. An `out_of_scope` protocol only emits a construction-time warning in `qkdx/protocol/base.py` and is then solved normally. I verified that a dummy `scope_tag="out_of_scope"` protocol is accepted and returns a numeric rate. This directly contradicts RESEARCH_PLAN R1.4 / `docs/framework_coverage.md`, so an invalid protocol can silently receive a publishable-looking key rate instead of being rejected.
issues.suggestion: Add a hard gate at solver entry: raise an `OutOfScopeError`/`ValueError` for `scope_tag == "out_of_scope"`, and make `partial` either explicit opt-in or at least a runtime warning. Add a regression test that `wlc_key_rate()` refuses an out-of-scope dummy protocol.

issues.description: The multi-source MS-EB API is not implemented, but `build_mdi_protocol()` still claims `scope_tag="covered"`. `joint_state()` and `executed_state()` only use `self.sources[0]`; on MDI this means `joint_state()` returns Alice’s 8-vector instead of the combined two-source state, and `executed_state()` crashes with a dimension mismatch because the network expects `A'⊗B'` (dim 4) while only one source state is propagated. So the “channel absorbed into `_conditional_alice_bob` override” shortcut does break the advertised MS-EB semantics even though the idealized WLC path happens to return the expected rate.
issues.suggestion: Either implement true multi-source state construction/evolution (tensor the source states and apply Charlie’s map on the joint signal space), or downgrade MDI to `scope_tag="partial"` and make unsupported state queries raise clearly. Add tests that call `joint_state()`, `executed_state()`, and `conditional_alice_bob()` on the MDI protocol.

issues.description: The Frank-Wolfe fallback does not keep its iterate exactly feasible. `_init_feasible()` solves the equality-constrained SDP and then adds `1e-8 I` plus renormalization, which perturbs the observation constraints. The subsequent FW loop then mixes an infeasible point with feasible subproblem solutions, so the reported `duality_gap` at lines 243-247 is no longer a valid Frank-Wolfe certificate; in direct checks it becomes negative, and the returned `optimal_rho` misses the target observables by about `1e-8`. This undermines the documented gap/tolerance semantics of the fallback solver.
issues.suggestion: Keep the iterate exactly on the affine constraint set and regularize only the `logm` evaluation (or project the perturbed point back onto the constraints before iterating). Only interpret/report the FW gap after feasibility is guaranteed, and add regression tests asserting nonnegative gap plus small constraint residuals at `QBER=0` and near threshold.

issues.description: `compute_face_projector()` silently treats some infeasible zero-target PSD constraints as if they caused no reduction. If `A_restricted` has no kernel, the constraint `Tr(Aρ)=0` with `A ⪰ 0` is incompatible with any nonzero PSD state on the current face, but the code just `continue`s and eventually returns the current projector. Example: `A = I, b = 0` should yield an empty feasible set, yet the function returns the full-rank identity projector. That is not the stated kernel-intersection algorithm and can mask contradictory constraints.
issues.suggestion: When a zero-target PSD constraint has empty kernel in the current face, signal infeasibility explicitly (exception or dedicated status/rank-0 result) instead of continuing. Add a regression test for `A = I, b = 0` and a near-singular tolerance case.

issues.description: The decoy suite does not lock in the regression criterion called out in the review brief. `test_2decoy_close_to_1decoy_numerically()` only checks that `ν₂ → 0` makes the 2-decoy rate roughly match the 1-decoy rate; it would still pass if the previously observed “2-decoy > 1-decoy” benchmark regression reappeared at the actual reproducer parameter set. The decoy/WLC integration tests also do not pin boundary behavior around the distance threshold.
issues.suggestion: Add the exact reproducer from the prior regression as a pinned test on fixed `(L, μ, ν₁, ν₂)` values, asserting the intended 1-decoy vs 2-decoy ordering/range for that benchmark. Also add threshold-edge tests with assert messages that print the actual `R`, `Y_1^L`, and `e_1^U` values.

round_recommendation: First hard-block `out_of_scope` protocols at solver entry and either implement or downgrade the MDI multi-source semantics. Then repair Frank-Wolfe feasibility/gap handling and facial-reduction infeasibility detection, and finally add the missing decoy regression tests.
